cards.meaning: A block that iterates a list of commands as long as the loop control condition is true
cards.notes: Control condition decides whether another pass runs.

cards.meaning: On each pass, arg takes the value of the next item in the list
cards.example: for arg in one two three; do echo "$arg"; done
cards.notes: One pass per list item. Use when you already have the list.

cards.front: for file in "$(find . -type l)"; do …; done | sort
cards.meaning: Build the for-list from command output (here: symlinks under .), then sort the loop’s output
cards.example:
for file in "$( find . -type l )"; do
  echo "$file"
done | sort
cards.notes: find . -type l lists symbolic links. The pipe applies to the whole loop’s stdout.

cards.example: for i in {1..5}; do echo $i; done

cards.meaning: Test at the top; keep looping while the condition is true (exit status 0)
cards.example:
LIMIT=10
while [ "$a" -le $LIMIT ]; do
  echo -n "$a "
  let "a+=1"
done
cards.notes: Use when the number of repetitions is not known beforehand. Give counters a starting value (empty "$a" is not a number).

cards.meaning: Opposite of while — test at the top; loop while the condition is false; stop when true (status 0)
cards.notes: while = repeat while true. until = repeat until true (while false). Same do / done.

cards.meaning: for = known list, one pass per item; while = condition-driven when the count is unknown
cards.example: for x in list · while [ cond ]
cards.notes: until is the false-side twin of while.

cards.meaning: Terminate the loop — break out of it
cards.example:
for i in {1..5}; do
  echo $i
  [[ $i -eq 3 ]] && break
done
# prints 1 2 3
cards.notes: echo runs before break, so 3 prints; 4 and 5 never run.

cards.meaning: Jump to the next iteration — skip the remaining commands in this cycle
cards.notes: Does not leave the loop. In the {1..5} break example, continue in that same spot would still print 1–5 (nothing follows the [[ … ]] line).
